data.description:
Prerequisite epic for the test creation calibration program (d566-afa6, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39, 411b-a047). Introduces a structural separation between end-state intent (SC/DoD/AC — durable, behavior-describing, test-target-worthy) and transitional/work intent (one-time migrations, deletions, refactors completed during the sprint).

## Problem

Today, SC/DoD/AC sections mix two kinds of items:
- End-state intent — durable property of the system; worth a persistent test. Example: 'Users can export results as CSV.'
- Transitional/work intent — one-time achievement during the sprint; becomes a change-detector the day after closure. Example: 'All 23 callers of legacy_export() have been migrated.'

Mixing the two pollutes the test-claim pool (downstream of intent allocation epic). Any structural test-allocation system inherits the pollution unless we cleave them at the schema level.

## Goal

Restructure the epic/story/task description templates so that:
- '## Success Criteria' (epic), '## Definition of Done' (story), '## Acceptance Criteria' (task) sections contain **end-state intent only**.
- A new '## Closure Checks' section (applicable at all three levels at appropriate granularity) contains transitional/work intent that the completion verifier checks once at closure and then discards.
- The verifiable-SC check (skills/shared/prompts/verifiable-sc-check.md) gains an end-state-only rule: rejects items with completion-language ('has been migrated', 'is now using', 'is removed') and routes them to Closure Checks.

## Scope of migration (touchpoint audit)

This is the highest-blast-radius epic in the calibration program. Audit and update all sites that reference Success Criteria / Definition of Done / Acceptance Criteria semantics:

- ~40 skill files across brainstorm/, preplanning/, implementation-plan/, sprint/, roadmap/, retro/, prioritize-epics/, design-review/, ui-designer/, shared/.
- 9 scripts: validate-review-output.sh, ticket-lib-api.sh, ticket-clarity-check.sh, issue-quality-check.sh, ticket-next-batch.sh, issue-batch.sh, ticket CLI, classify-task.py, check-acceptance-criteria.sh.
- Agents: code-reviewer-deep-correctness.md and any other reviewer/verifier that reads SC/DoD/AC.
- Contracts: new contract for closure-checks-block; updates to any existing contract referencing SC validation.
- Completion verifier: largest functional change. New responsibilities — (a) read Closure Checks separately from end-state intent, (b) validate each end-state item via the intent-allocation manifest (owner_ticket exists, registered test_artifact exists and passes), (c) recursively validate the entire descendant subtree before allowing a parent ticket to close.

## Migration safety

Risk: reducing intent-capture fidelity during the migration. Mitigations:
- Dual-read period — completion verifier accepts legacy tickets (no Closure Checks section) by treating all SC/DoD/AC items as end-state; new tickets are required to use v2 schema.
- Per-ticket schema version flag.
- Migration sentinel: before/after diff on a representative set of in-flight epics to prove no end-state item was misclassified as transitional or vice versa.
- Closure Checks section is required at the epic level; optional at story/task level where there is no transitional work at that granularity.

## Out of scope

- Plan-time intent allocation manifest (separate prerequisite epic, depends on this).
- Test-writing prompt rules (d566-afa6, depends on this).
- Test-growth metrics (7f42-e41f).
- Mutation infrastructure (411b-a047).

## Dependents

d566-afa6, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39, 411b-a047, and the intent-allocation prerequisite epic (to be created) all depend on this schema cleavage.

Refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Closure Checks schema migration: separate end-state intent from transitional work across all planning artifacts
